dynamicViews.description: Reading one application. It runs once per case, and the answers are stored.
dynamicViews.name: Dynamic View: Permit Engine - Engine

relationships.description: Open the application: The Reader loads the form, the cover letter and the attachments of one case.
Basic checks: Is the fee paid, is the form complete, is the date allowed? A failure stops the case here, before any model is called.

Link and extract: In the first pass, for each kind of proof a race can need, the LLM says found or absent, gives fields with quotes, and lists documents that fit no kind. This is the only pass that reads the cover letter.

Quote check: Each quote must appear in the named attachment and each value inside its quote, or the field counts as absent. The form and the cover letter are never allowed as sources, so a letter cannot become evidence.

Judge: In the second pass, in a fresh context, the LLM gets the attachments behind verified fields and the case's typed values, never the cover letter. It gives one verdict per kind of proof: supported, unsupported or contradicted.
Hazard screen: By rules only, traffic applies if a road closes, crowd pressure if the crowd is 300 or more, and medical always.

Tree questions: One Jev request per case, with typed values, evidence records and whole plan documents. Jev returns a probability for each question on the hazards that apply. It never sees the cover letter.
Store the answers: All of this becomes one reading record. From here on, the case needs no model call.

dynamicViews.description: Deciding one case. No model is called, so any decision can be reproduced.
dynamicViews.name: Dynamic View: Permit Engine - Engine

relationships.description: Pick up the case: The Run builder hands the case to the pipeline, with the weights and thresholds of the moment.
Load the reading record: The pipeline starts from the stored answers, not from a new model call.
Compare fields with the form: Code compares each extracted field with the form. A mismatch, such as a letter naming another date, makes the record contradicted whatever the LLM said.
Requirements and rule answers: Rego gives each requirement a status (met, failed, missing or unclear), and answers every question the form can settle.
Work out the risk: Answers send the case down up to six trees. Each hazard's likelihood times its severity, summed over the hazards that apply, gives the risk.
Apply the decision table: Rego reads the table from the top, and the first match wins: returned, proposed denial, officer or approved, with the row, the reason and the clause.
Log the decision: Every stage is written as an event, with the hashes of everything the decision used. If the write fails, the decision does not take effect.

dynamicViews.description: An officer reviews a case, and the trees learn from it.
dynamicViews.name: Dynamic View: Permit Engine - Engine

relationships.description: Send it to review: Every case except a returned form goes on. A case sent to an officer gets a ruling, and any other case gets a review of what the system did.

The officer rules: The officer sees the documents, the decision, the risk and the trees to give a level for. They return a ruling, risky or not, a one-line reason and a level per tree. A real deployment would use a person. In this demo an LLM stands in, always labelled as simulated.
Log the ruling: The ruling is logged with who made it. A permit is only issued with a logged decision or ruling as its parent.

Teach the trees: Every review teaches, not only disagreements. A Bayesian network works back from the outcome and the named levels, and adds shares to the counts on the leaves this case reached, after discounting their old counts.
Log the new weights: The new weights version is logged. If the review disagreed with the system's estimate, it is also logged as a correction, with old and new values.
Re-choose the thresholds: At a set interval of reviews, the two thresholds are chosen again, because thresholds fitted to one set of weights do not fit the next.
Decide the next case: Later cases use the new weights and thresholds, and each records the version it used.

dynamicViews.description: A person makes a change official.
dynamicViews.name: Dynamic View: Permit Engine - Engine

relationships.description: Edit a rule file: A change is data, not code: a tree question, a setting or a first guess. A lint command checks the rule files, and a setting outside its limits stops the run.
Fit a candidate: The policy owner runs train and thresholds. Models are not called again.
Read the stored answers: Fitting reads the answers already stored for each case, so it makes no model call.
Write the candidate: Candidate weights and thresholds are written beside the released ones. Nothing uses them yet.
Read the result: The policy owner reads the candidate's validation result, and either releases it or leaves it.
Release: The policy owner runs release under a new version name.
Keep every version: Release copies the candidate to the new version, with the role and the hashes it was fitted on. Released versions never change in place, and it refuses to overwrite one.

dynamicViews.description: A finished run reaches a visitor, and any decision in it can be checked.
dynamicViews.name: Dynamic View: Permit Engine - Engine

relationships.description: Read the finished run: The Exporter reads the log of one finished run.
Write static files: It writes the run as JSON and scans every file for vendor names and keys. Only then does it replace the old folder.
Serve one folder: A plain file server sends that folder. It holds no keys and runs no application code.
Open the page: Any visitor can open the replay and any case, with no login. There are no action buttons.
Play the run: The browser loads the JSON and plays the run. Nothing is computed for the visitor, and no model is called.
Pick a decision to check: The replay command reads a logged decision and the hashes of what it used.
Run it again: It reruns the decision with no model calls and checks that the result is identical. It refuses if the rules, the settings, the application or the arithmetic have changed.
